target_customer: Web developers and startups building full-stack React and Node apps
problem: Building full-stack web apps requires heavy boilerplate for auth, CRUD and jobs.
business_model: Open source framework with planned paid hosting and services

founders.name: Martin Sosic
founders.background_notes: Authored the Edlib library per the YC page. Twin brother of Matija per TechCrunch.

technical_complexity.rationale: A compiler and DSL generating full-stack apps across React, Node and Prisma.

defensibility.rationale: Open source with some lock-in to the config language but easy to fork or replace.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: AI coding tools reduced boilerplate pain by 2025, though Wasp grew via Open SaaS.

market_need_then: Developers wanted less boilerplate; TechCrunch reported about 300 apps built on the alpha in 2021.

identity.mascot_or_character: Boi mascot drawn by Zeke Boinanza

branding.community_and_virality: Open SaaS reached over 10,000 GitHub stars and Discord has 4,669 members per an AI Engineer profile; launch weeks and a mascot design contest.

brand_strength.rationale: Friendly name and community but name is generic and confusable with other Wasp products.

outcome_analysis: Wasp raised a $1.5M seed in 2021, built an open source framework and grew through the Open SaaS template to 26,000 GitHub stars. A $3.7M round closed in late 2024 and total raised is $5.2M. The team is small, about eight people, and has not shown a revenue model yet.
notes: Website wasp-lang.dev fetch was rate limited; used YC page and wasp.sh blog results instead. 2024 round: TechCrunch says closed late 2024 and previously unannounced; seedtable calls it a 2025 seed; stage set to other. Blitz.js listed from an undated pkgpulse comparison, source_date uses TechCrunch article date; weak.
